Do I understand that the timber, not having been creosoted, has been eaten by the worms V
Yes, it was eaten away by the worms before the work was completed.

The hon. minister says he intends to have a creosotiug plant. Where will it bo located ?
!
The MINISTER Oh' PUBLIC WORKS. I cannot tell at present-somewhere in the maritime provinces.
Great Salmon river-Groin and breakwater combined, $4,300.
Is that Great Salmon river on the Bay of Fundy coast ?
Yes.
Is this a new work ?
Yes.
Is it to be built by contract ?
Yes.
Has the contract been let ?

Not yet.
Little Salmon river beach protection works, $S00.
Is that Little Salmon river on the Bay of Fundy coast also ?

Yes.
Partridge Island-repairs to eastern pier, $1,200.
Is it proposed by the government to go on with the dredging works at the entrance to the harbour ?

We have no dredge available for that large work. We might find a dredge, but tlie cost of the work with the dredges now available is so high that the government has decided to postpone the dredging of St. John harbour until the new dredge, which is now under construction, is completed.
Where is it being built ?
In the government shipyard at Sorel.
Would not the latest-built . dredge, the one turned out at Toronto, do the work ?

That would not be available as a sea-going dredge; it is for the St. Lawrence channel.
River St. John-wharf at Oromocto, $5,500.
Is that a new work ?
Yes.
Has the minister secured a site for the wharf ?
We have not a site yet, but we are preparing to buy one. The plans are ready for
the work, and tenders will be asked for as soon as we have a site.
I believe it was stated some time ago that $6,500 would be appropriated for the work.

We have $1,500 in the main estimates.
Wharfs on tidal waters on the St. John river and tributaries, $5,000.
Could the hon. gentleman tell me what wharfs there are in King's county ?
Jenkin's wharf, Oak Point wharf, Beilyea's Cove wharf and Rothesay wharf.
When will tenders be called for Oromooto ?
There will be no delay.
When will a dredge suitable for St. John harbour be sent ?

By the opening of next season, I hope.
Ratiscan river-To continue the dredging of a channel at outlet of river, $10,000.
How much has been spent on that ?
This will complete the work, which will have amounted to $20,000. We have no dredge of our own suitable for that work, and have had to hire a dredge, for which we pay $8 an hour.
Has the minister called for any offers from different people to do this work, or does he make a contract with some individual ?

We do not always call for tenders. We give $8 an hour in this case, provided the dredge does 600 yards a day, and when the dredge does not do that much, we deduct the difference. The dredging costs us 301 cents a yard. It is the cheapest way we can do the work. Next year I think we will be able to dispense with all these outside dredges.
How is this work supervised ?
Not only have we got local inspectors, but we have district engineers who oversee the work.

I have been told that there are places where the overseer goes around town while the dredging is going on. Who keeps account of what work is being done ? I am credibly informed that there are many instances where there is no overseer at all. and the account is kept by the owner of the dredge himself.
I would be surprised to get evidence of that state of affairs. As a rule, I am prepared to say that our overseers are well chosen.
Is the local inspector in charge of this work a man of experience ?

The chief engineer informs me that this man has been with us two years and is a very able man.
Crane Island, south side, heavy repairs to wharf, $3,500.
Where is Crane Island ?

In the St. Lawrence, below Quebec.
Cross Point-isolated landing pier (revote), $5,000.
Is this contract work?
Yes.
What is the meaning of an isolated landing pier ?
An isolated pier means a block constructed which is not connected with the shore.
It stands out from the shore ?

Quite so. When we find that it will be too expensive to build from the shore we build an isolated block.
Maria-isolated block, $12,000.
As this is a pretty large item the hon. minister had better explain it.

We had $12,000 in the estimates last year. We asked for tenders and the lowest tender that came in was $24,000. Maria is one of the most important parishes on the Baie de Chaleur. There was no wharf at that place. The nearest wharf was Carleton on one side and New Carlisle on the other. It was found to be too expensive to build a wharf on the shore. Then, we made up our minds to prepare plans for an isolated block. There are regular lines of steamers navigating in those waters. It is to enable these steamers and the schooners which call there to load and unload that we are building that block. This will complete .the work, and it is being done by tender and contract.
I do not quite understand what you mean by an isolated block. It means. I presume, that the wharf stands away from the shore ?
Quite so.
Then how do you get to the shore-by small boats ?

By boat. We have several of these in the St. Lawrence.
Magdalen Island-breakwaters, additional, $14,300.
What is the total expenditure ?

That will complete the work. The total expenditure, this Item included, will be $32,000. Plans were prepared for a more expensive work. I visited the work, myself, with the chief engineer, and we reduced the plans to a moderate sum, three years ago.
I'Ointe Fortune-wharf, $5,000.
Is this a new work ?
It is a new work in this way, that there is an old work and we will include a new work in it.
Does this complete it ?
Yes.
Is it by contract ?

No, it will be a kind of repair work.
Point St. Pierre-breakwater, $5,000.
Is this uew ?
Yes, by contract. We have already a, vote of $5,000.
That will be $10,000 altogether ?
Yes.
AArill that complete it ?
No.
AVhat will be the total cost ?
$14,000 is the estimate.
Is the work let by contract ?
By contract.
AVhere is it ?

In the county of Gaspe. There are about 200 fishing schooners visiting that place. It is one of the most important points in the county of Gaspe from the fisherman's standpoint, and there is also considerable local trade. They have no railway in that part of the country.
Riviere aux Renards-pier, $10,000.
By contract.
I
Where is this ?
In Gaspe also, on the north shore.
Is this a new work ?
No, it is the continuation of an old work.
How much has been expended already ?	.
Six thousand dollars has been spent already and this will complete the work; by contract.

(Translation.) Mr. Chairman, as a section of the county Which 1 represent here is concerned in this vote, I think it my duty to call the attention of the Minister of Public Works to the harbour of Riviere du Loup, which is daily increasing in importance. The Fraser firm, of New Brunswick, have been building shanties and saw-mills on the shores of Lake Temis-eouata, and they are exporting annually to Great Britain large quantities of lumber. That lumber has to be shipped from Riviere du Louip. But unfortunately, there is no accommodation on the wharf and their ships have to load and unload toy small boats away from the shore. Of course that entails a considerable loss of time, which would be remedied if we had, at Riviere du Loup, a wharf in deep water. I know that surveys and plans have been made by the engineer, Mr. Auclair. I should be very glad if the hon. minister would kindly communicate those plans to the Chamber of Commerce of Fraserville, as also the report of Mr. Fraser, the engineer of the Public AVorks Department, with alii the plans, maps, specifications and cost of the works, in connection with the building of a wharf at Riviere du Loup.

(Translation.) My hon. friend has just called attention to conditions which are not peculiar to RiviSre du Loup, but which exist in all the places along the St. Lawrence where lumber cargoes are handled. The ships have to load and unload by means of small boats. I should feel most happy were I able to build wharfs everywhere, tout my hon. friend will easily understand that such works involve a large expenditure of money. I cannot commit myself to any such policy for the future, until I have all the desirable data and information before me.
I shall be very happy to communicate to the Chamber of Commerce of Fraserville the report of the engineer Who has made the survey referred to.
St. Francois-breakwater, wharf on the south shore of the Island of Orleans, $10,000.
speakername: The MINISTER OF PUBLIC AVORKS (Mr. Tarte).

speechtext: Will this complete the work ?
I do not think it will cost more than that. The work will be of great local importance, and it is necessary also in view of the dredging operations we will carry on opposite Crane Island.
What use will the minister have for a wharf on the south side of the island ?

I have just said that St. Francois is a very important parish and we are going to dredge at Crane Island, which is a very stormy place, and our dredges and scows will be obliged to find shelter there.

On the north shore there has been a whanf for a great many years and you never see any kind of boat stop there, and on the south shore there is no line of steamers at all. I have passed that place time and again and there is no traffic there. Did I understand the minister to say that Crane Island was opposite that place ?
No. At Crane Island there is no shelter, and our dredges and scows would be obliged to come here in a storm.
I do not find any fault with building wharfs where they are necessary, but it is not necessary here.

I am afraid the hon. gentleman has not given this question his best attention. He must know that there is no line of steamers on the north side of the island, and the fact is that the wharf built there by the Conservative government was badly located and was of no use at all. There is a line of steamers visiting St. Laurent and St. Jean, and when this wharf is completed these steamers will call at St. Francois.
I cannot agree with the minister on that point, because the Richelieu and Ontario Company's steamer that leaves Quebec goes to Bay St. Paul on the north shore.
Always on the south shore. The hon. gentleman is mistaken.
He is not.
It is well known that a steamer never goes by the north channel.
The Richelieu boats go by the north channel.
Never.

Well, that just shows you don't know what you are talking about neither. There is a time to joke, but there is no time to say things that are not so. When I took the boat at Quebec for the Saguenay, I knew where I was going.
The hon. gentleman went by the south channel and not by the north channel.

I said that the Richelieu Navigation boats go by the south channel, and the minister said that this was not the case. I say it is the case. I also went from Quebec to Bay St. Paul on the north channel, on a boat called ' The Brother.'
Oh, that is a small boat.

It makes no difference liow big it is or how little. I say I went on the north channel and the south channel too, and you cannot fool me on that. I am not here to brag like the Minister of Justice, who thinks that he knows better than I do things I have seen myself. Well, it is for him to say it and for me not to believe him.
St. Irenee wharf-construction of head block,
What is the necessity for this ?
St. Irenee is one of those places which is developing a large summer trade indeed, and this is to accommodate that trade. -
Will it be done by contract ?
Yes.
Will this complete ?

Yes.
St. John do Chaillons-improvement of harbour, $2,000.
Will the minister explain this ?

That is a mistake. We have dredged there to the solid rock bottom, and now- that we have reached the hard material it would require a much larger sum to go on with the work. This item cannot be used this year.
Then why leave it in ?
It cannot be used this year, and I move that it be struck out.

Motion agreed to.
St. Laurent wharf-Island of Orleans. $4,000.
What is this for ?
St. Laurent is one of the most important parishes on the Island of Orleans, and this is to extend the work already] there.

With respect to ali these wharfs in the maritime provinces,

as well as in Quebec and Ontario, is there any system of wharfages, or is the use of these wharfs given free to the public ?
When we have completed a wharf we transfer it to the Department of Marine and Fisheries, and it then becomes subject to the general law. We have nothing more to do with it.
What is the general law 1
I really cannot explain it as it is not in my department.

The general law, as I understand it, is simply this, that the town or municipality in which the wharf is situated passes a by-law regulating the wharfage dues, and that is ratified here. I ought to know this because I have had two or three Bills for that purpose put through the House. Where private individuals build wharfs they usually charge such wharfage (dues as they see fit, and these are sometimes rather onerous on shipping. I think there should be some kind of supervision over all these charges by the government.

I only referred to wharfs built by us. The owners of private wharfs generally exact what charges they like, but there is a general tariff that applies everywhere to wharfs built out of the public exchequer.

Take the wharf at Thorn-bury. That was built out of the public exchequer aided by the municipality, but the municipality passed a by-law regulating the wharfage 'dues and this was ratified and made legal here.

I understand that the wharf at Thornbury has been constructed by the municipality and the federal government jointly. It is an exceptional case, but I speak of wharfs which are constructed altogether out of the public exchequer. When they are completed we transfer them to the Department of Marine and Fisheries.

There is scarcely one completed entirely out of the public exchequer. At Collingwood, Meaford and Owen Sound there are wharfs constructed in the same way, the municipality giving a portion of the cost and the government the rest.
Are there charges on all these wharfs ?
Oh, yes.
Do these charges go in to the public exchequer ?

Yes.
Mi1. BORDEN (Halifax). What amount of wharfage charges was collected during the past year ?
That I cannot say. The Department of Marine and Fisheries has charge of that part of the work.
Where is the Minister of Marine and Fisheries ?
I suppose he is busy somewhere in the public interest.
Can the Minister of Finance tell us ?
There was between $10,000 and $11,000 received last year from all over the Dominion. They vary. Some of the wharfs yield quite a respectable sum.
Are they collected with regularity.
I am not prepared to answer that question. The Department of Marine looks after the collections.
The wharfingers get 25 per cent on what they collect and have to make the small repairs, between $10 and $15 a year.

The reason 1 inquire is because I have received communications now and then, stating that the people in charge of these wharfs have not remitted to the government anything on account of the wharfage dues they have received for a long time. I prefer to ask for that information in this general way rather than to take up the time of the government by moving for a special return, but we ought to have some information as to the system adopted, and find out whether or not these statements I have referred to are really founded in fact.
If my hon. friend will send me the names of the wharfs, I will have an inquiry made. He need not necessarily give the names of the complainants.

The wharfs to which the government appoint wharfingers only represent very few of the total number. As a general thing the municipalities receive assistance from the government to build the wharfs and then get the revenue themselves, and are supposed to keep them in repair, but may put the revenue into the municipal exchequer.
In my short experience, 1 have come across some cases of the kind referred to by the hon. member for Halifax, and we are making a general review of the whole situation. Twenty-five per cent is
speakername: The MINISTER OF MARINE AND FISHERIES.

speechtext: allowed the wharfingers, and in some cases where the revenues are very small, they are allowed as high as 50 per cent. In others where the revenue is large, they are paid a salary. I am having the whole matter looked into and will be able to give the House full information next session.

Considering the enormous expenditure on these wharfs, the sum of $10,000 or $12,000 seems to be a very small amount to be received from them in the shape of revenue. Some general system should be devised for the collection of the wharfage dues. A rigid system should be applied to all wharfs alike, because otherwise one part of the country may be getting the benefit of these wharfs for nothing, while in another part the wharfage dues may be exacted regularly and systematically. This is a matter which demands the immediate attention of the lion. Minister of Marine in order that a thorough system be applied all over the country without any discrimination in favour of any particular locality.
Amherstburg, Ontario-dredging (revote), $5,-
000.
Is this by contract or day's work ?

We will try to do it with our own dredge. There are boulders to be removed there also.
Big Bay, Ontario (North Keppel), wharf-repairs, $500.
What wharf is that ?
This is in North Grey. It is to replank the wharf, and this sum is applied for by the resident engineer.
That is not the one struck out in the main estimates ?

No, it is not the same work at all.
Burke's Falls' Magnetawan river-wharf, $4,500.
Will this be let by contract ?

Yes.
Burlington channel-repairs to piers-To complete works under contracts (additional revote, $20,000), $50,000.
Is this intended to complete it ?
Yes, this will complete the work now under contract.
What is the work ?

My hon. friend knows that the port of Hamilton is becoming more and more important on account of the large smelting operations there. The port is composed of a large bay, the entrance to which has been made by two long jetties. Unfortunately, they were built in wood and have to be repaired without delay. We are simply rebuilding the principal structure.
In wood again ?

Yes, I was afraid to ask parliament for concrete. When I started the work years ago, 1 was younger than now, and was afraid to ask parliament for the larger amount which would have been required if the work had been done with concrete. Moreover, the foundations of most of those works in Ontario have been laid in the quicksand and without the care that we take now. They have foundations only twelve feet deep. In other words, we can not dredge near the jetty without endangering it. We are obliged to make a tunnel in the middle of the stream.
Is this contract let ?

Yes, and the work is going on.
Callendar-repairs to wharf, $1,500.
Where is this ?

On Lake Nipissing, at the terminus of the Grand Trunk Railway.
Cobourg

rep lira to oiors and dredging, $10,-
000.

This is to complete the work.
Collingwood-dredging, $45,000.
What condition is Collingwood harbour in now ?

I gave an explanation on the main estimates, but I do not mind stating the case again. The channel we have dredged into the harbour is now 110 feet wide and 20 feet deep. We are deepening it to 200 feet, so as to allow the large ships that are seeking that harbour to come in and out without danger.
Will you make the channel 200 feet wide for the whole length ?
No, only the entrance where there is danger of the waves throwing the boats against the sides of the dredged channel.
When does the hon. minister expect this money to be used up V

We expect this to be spent during the next fiscal year. I may say that Mr. Boone, who is carrying on that work, is well equipped. It has been carried on with great success,
4G39

and the result, my hon. friend (Mr. Sproule) will agree, is very satisfactory. Large shipyards are being built at Collingwood, new lumbering operations, and so on. That little town is growing up pretty fast.

The work is a very important one, as the place is going to be a very, important place. Because, as the hon. minister says, new works are springing up. The largest meat curing establishment in the Dominion is there, and shipyards, saw mills, iron works and other large establishments are being provided. The place is growing very rapidly, and the work carried on by the government has been much needed. Has the hon. minister taken into consideration the application of the people of Collingwood with regard to their dry dock ? Their dry dock was built many years ago, but it is now too short and there is not enough depth of water to accommodate the large ships that use the liarhour. I understand that the government give two per cent on the cost of dry docks built, but the people of Collingwood feel that more is required. Dry docks are very costly, and they are not a very paying property. I think the government should give more assistance to provide a dry dock at Collingwood. Has the minister considered the question, and has he decided to do anything ?

There is a law on the statute-book to the effect that when any private corporation is desirous of building a graving dock they may submit their plans to the government, and when these plans are approved they may enter into a contract with the government, and then they become entitled to a guarantee of two per cent for twenty years. Mr. Long, from Collingwood, or rather the Northern Navigation Company, applied for that subsidy, which, after I had examined the plans, I recommended my colleagues to grant. That is the present position of the question. I am confident that with the two per cent subsidy the company will be able to go on. although I am not quite sure of it. I fully recognize the great importance of it or rather the great necessity of having a grain dock on the lakes capable of accommodating the large boats navigating those waters. So far as I am concerned, and if there is a hitch in the matter, I shall be glad to do all I can to overcome it.

I think the government would not be doing too much if they double the guarantee and made it four per cent, for it is very difficult to get men who have money to put it into such enterprise. Therefore, a great many boats are now compelled to go away for repairs, because they cannot get into the dry dock we have. With regard to the channel that has been made, I am told that it is answering the purpose very well, and the people feel extremely grateful for it. Towards the close of navigation last year they began to get in with Hon. Mr. TARTE.
large boats, loaded with grain, and I have no doubt that there will be an important trade in that line to Collingwood and also to Meaford-Meaford especially because of the important work done there, and because they have a good elevator at Meaford. They have an elevator at Collingwood also, but not quite so good as that at Meaford. In both places they have 'been able to take advantage of their harbour during the last year owing to the expenditure made-a wise expenditure, I quite believe. There will be a very important trade done there, not only during the present season tout for the future also we hope.

The sooner the people of this country realize the great benefits to be derived from the improvements and equipment of their harbour the better. Unfortunately, perhaps, there are not enough public men who give their attention to that important question. I think that every harbour on Georgian Bay should be fully equipped, and I have no doubt that when that is done there will be trade for them all.

I am sure there will.
Georgian hay-Pointe an Baril routs-improvement of the Devil's Elbow channel between Parry Sound and Killarney, $3,000.
What is the nature of the work to be done there ? Is it to be crib-work, blasting or dredging ?

Blasting and the removal of shoals. I do not think it is necessary to have any crib-work there. This is a most dangerous part, and I am carrying out the work at the request of the Navigation Company.
Goderich harbour works, $6,000.
What is the hon. minister doing there ?
We are completing the repairs to the jetties in the inside of the harbour. Goderich is also getting a large traffic, I am glad to say. and the money spent there for repairs has been well invested.
With Dan McGillicuddy as superintendent.
Well, he was the lowest tenderer.
I am not objecting.

I am glad that the hon. gentleman is satisfied.
Hilton, St. Joseph's island-wharf repairs, ?!,-500.
Is that a private dock ?

No, a public dock.

Huntsville-new wharf, $3,500.
Does the hon. gentleman intend to do that work by contract ?

Yes.
Midland harbour-wharf, $10,000.

This is a work to accommodate the public generally. The citizens without distinction of party have applied to me and I could not resist their request. Midland is a thriving town and the corporation is going to give us the site. There is only one site on which to build the wharf now and the town has bought it and offered it to us.
Orillia-new wharf, $3,000.
This is where the ladies attacked the hon. gentleman with their seductive smiles and he succumbed to them.
I stand ready to be captured again.
I would like the minister to come up to Parry Sound,*a town which he has neglected very badly. Perhaps the ladies there will be able to induce him to build a dock.
What is the new work to be done at Orillia ?

It is an ordinary wharf, costing $5,000 or $6,000. The work is let by contract.
Penetanguisihene-dredging, $10,000.
Have you any dredges on Georgian Bay ?
Unfortunately we have no dredges there.

I spoke last night with reference to a gentleman who is writing to me that he has a splendid suction dredge that he would be glad to bring out any time the Minister of Public Works required it. It is only in the case of the government having no dredges of their own available that I would recommend bringing in American dredges. Rather than have these places suffer for want of such a work, I think the minister would be quite justified in hir

 ing a dredge from any source.

I may say that a suction dredge would not do in this place. They can only work in soft material and at Penetanguishene it is hard material.
Port Elgin-repairs to lauding pier, extension of breakwater and dredging, $5,000.
$5,000 will not go far here. What kind of work are you doing there ?

The chief engineer is afraid that this amount 146
of money will not be sufficient to accomplish the objects both of completing the pier and doing the dredging. It will complete the pier, and we will have to draw on our general vote to carry out the dredging. It is intended to let the contract to build the pier.
South Nation river-improvements at the pitch off, $1,000.

I understand this is for the purpose of preventing the flooding of the land. The question has been raised whether, if the government adopts the principle of doing this kind of work here, other places in the country will not apply for the same assistance. I think the government will have other applications.

1 grant it is a bad place in which to do this kind of work. There are one or two items that are remnants of past days. I admit that the principle is wrong. But this river is navigable, at least I was drawn into this work on the representation that it is a navigable river. But this will not appear again.
Lake St. Francis outlet-construction of guide pier end dredging (revote, $1,200), $6,500.
Is that where the St. Francis river empties into the lake ?

Yes.
Winnipegosis-dredging channel at mouth of the Mossy river, $4,500.
I do not see any item here, but I would like to ask the hon. minister what he is doing now with the St. Andrews' rapids. Is the work going on there ?

We have an item in the main estimates, but I am sorry to say that the contractors are not going on very speedily with the work. I instructed my officers a few days ago to give notice to the Messrs. Kelly Bros, that they would have to go on with the work or the contract would be taken off their hands.

Hardy bay-wharf, $2,00i.

Is this the amount that the hon. minister said would surprise me when I would see the supplementary estimates for British Columbia ?
*
I hope I did not say that this would surprise the hou. gentleman.

I am surprised at the smallness of the amount, because on the west coast of Vancouver island there are no wharfs and there should be some expenditures, on that part of the coast. The steamers running on the west coast of Vancouver island have, with one or two exceptions, where there are private wharfs, to land their passengers by small boats. More money can be spent with a greater advantage to the settlers at various points on the west coast of Vancouver island.

All I can say is that this is only a beginning. My hon. friend (Mr. Earle) has been a long time in parliament. If he had applied in past days, I have no doubt lie would have received more than lias been spent there. This is the first demand for wharfs that has come to me. It is a beginning. I do not want to encourage anybody to come, but if there are legitimate requests from British Columbia they will be treated just as liberally as I always endeavour to treat legitimate demands that come to me.
Would the hon. minister consider a request coming from me as a legitimate request ?
I will be only too glad to consider in the most friendly and favourable manner any demand that may come from my bon. friend who is an old and respected member of this House.

We will see another session. There are several places where the bon. minister can spend money to good advantage.
